New Constructions of Binary Cyclic Codes with Both Relatively Large Minimum Distance and Dual Distance

Lingqi Zheng    Weijun Fang    Rongxing Qiu ††thanks: Lingqi Zheng, Weijun Fang and Rongxing Qiu are with State Key Laboratory of Cryptography and Digital Economy Security, Shandong University, Qingdao, 266237, China, Key Laboratory of Cryptologic Technology and Information Security, Ministry of Education, Shandong University, Qingdao, 266237, China and School of Cyber Science and Technology, Shandong University, Qingdao, 266237, China (email: zlingqihhh@outlook.com, fwj@sdu.edu.cn, qrx@mail.sdu.edu.cn). ††thanks: The work is supported in part by the National Key Research and Development Program of China under Grant Nos. 2022YFA1004900 and 2021YFA1001000, the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant No. 62201322, the Natural Science Foundation of Shandong Province under Grant No. ZR2022QA031, and the Taishan Scholar Program of Shandong Province. (Corresponding Author: Weijun Fang).††thanks: Manuscript submitted
Abstract

Binary cyclic codes are worth studying due to their applications and theoretical importance. It is an important problem to construct an infinite family of cyclic codes with large minimum distance dd and dual distance d⟂d^{\perp}. In recent years, much research has been devoted to improving the lower bound on dd, some of which have exceeded the square-root bound. The constructions presented recently seem to indicate that when the minimum distance increases, the minimum distance of its dual code decreases. In this paper, we focus on the new constructions of binary cyclic codes with length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1, dimension near n/2n/2, and both relatively large minimum distance and dual distance. For mm is even, we construct a family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1±1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}\pm 1,d], where d≥2m/2−1d\geq 2^{m/2}-1 and d⟂≥2m/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{m/2}. Both the minimum distance and the dual distance are significantly better than the previous results. When mm is the product of two distinct primes, we construct some cyclic codes with dimensions k=(n+1)/2k=(n+1)/2 and d>nlog2⁡n,d>\frac{n}{\log_{2}n}, where the lower bound on the minimum distance is much larger than the square-root bound. For mm is odd, we present two families of binary [2m−1,2m−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d] cyclic codes with d≥2(m+1)/2−1d\geq 2^{(m+1)/2}-1, d⟂≥2(m+1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m+1)/2} and d≥2(m+3)/2−15d\geq 2^{(m+3)/2}-15, d⟂≥2(m−1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2} respectively, which leads that d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp} can reach 2​n2n asymptotically. To the best of our knowledge, except for the punctured binary Reed-Muller codes, there is no other construction of binary cyclic codes that reaches this bound.

Index Terms: 
Binary codes, Cyclic codes, Cyclotomic coset, Minimum distance, Dual distance

I Introduction

Let 𝔽2n\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} be the nn-dimensional vector space over the finite field 𝔽2={0,1}\mathbb{F}_{2}=\left\{0,1\right\}. The Hamming weight w​t​(𝒂)wt(\bm{a}) of a vector 𝒂=(a0,a1,…,an−1)∈𝔽2n\bm{a}=(a_{0},a_{1},...,a_{n-1})\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} is the cardinality of the set s​u​p​p​(𝒂)={0≤i≤n−1:ai=1}.supp(\bm{a})=\left\{0\leq i\leq n-1:a_{i}=1\right\}. The Hamming distance d⁡(𝒂,𝒃)d(\bm{a},\bm{b}) between 𝒂\bm{a} and 𝒃\bm{b} is d⁡(𝒂,𝒃)=w​t​(𝒂−𝒃)d(\bm{a},\bm{b})=wt(\bm{a}-\bm{b}). For a code C⊂𝔽2nC\subset\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}, the minimum Hamming distance of CC is defined as

d=min𝒂≠𝒃{d(𝒂,𝒃):𝒂∈C,𝒃∈C}.d=\min_{\bm{a}\not=\bm{b}}\left\{d(\bm{a},\bm{b}):\bm{a}\in C,\bm{b}\in C\right\}.

An [n,k,d]2[n,k,d]_{2} linear code CC is a kk-dimensional linear subspace of 𝔽2n\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} with minimum Hamming distance dd. Let 𝒖=(u1,u2,…,un)∈𝔽2n\bm{u}=(u_{1},u_{2},...,u_{n})\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} and 𝒗=(v1,v2,..,vn)∈𝔽2n\bm{v}=(v_{1},v_{2},..,v_{n})\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}, the Euclidean inner product is defined as

⟨𝒖,𝒗⟩=∑i=1nui​vi,\langle\bm{u},\bm{v}\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^{n}u_{i}v_{i},

then the Euclidean dual code of CC is defined as

C⟂={𝒙∈𝔽2n:⟨𝒙,𝒄⟩=0,∀𝒄∈C}C^{\perp}=\left\{\bm{x}\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}:\langle\bm{x},\bm{c}\rangle=0,\forall\bm{c}\in C\right\}

and we denote the minimum distance of C⟂C^{\perp} as d⟂d^{\perp}, which is called as the dual distance of CC.

Cyclic codes were introduced by E. Prange in [1]. We say that an [n,k][n,k] linear code CC is cyclic if and only if for any 𝒄=(c0,c1,…,cn−1)∈C\bm{c}=(c_{0},c_{1},...,c_{n-1})\in C, we have (cn−1,c0,c1,…,cn−2)∈C.(c_{n-1},c_{0},c_{1},...,c_{n-2})\in C. Let nn be an odd integer and let CC be a binary cyclic code of length nn. A codeword 𝒄=(c0,c1,…,cn−1)\bm{c}=(c_{0},c_{1},...,c_{n-1}) in CC can be identified with the polynomial

c⁡(x)=c0+c1​x+⋯+cn−1​xn−1∈𝔽2​[x]/⟨xn−1⟩.c(x)=c_{0}+c_{1}x+\cdots+c_{n-1}x^{n-1}\in\mathbb{F}_{2}[x]/\langle x^{n}-1\rangle.

It is well known that every ideal of 𝔽2​[x]/⟨xn−1⟩\mathbb{F}_{2}[x]/\langle x^{n}-1\rangle is principal. Then there is a monic polynomial g​(x)∈𝔽2​[x]g(x)\in\mathbb{F}_{2}[x] with the smallest degree among all generators of CC. Clearly, g⁡(x)g(x) is unique and defined as the generator polynomial. Moreover, the dimension of CC dim⁡(C)=n−deg⁡(g⁡(x)){\rm{dim}}(C)=n-{\rm{deg}}(g(x)). Let h⁡(x)=xn−1g⁡(x)h(x)=\frac{x^{n}-1}{g(x)}, then the dual code C⟂C^{\perp} of CC is generated by

g⟂​(x)=xdim⁡(C)​h​(x−1)h⁡(0).g^{\perp}(x)=\frac{x^{{\rm{dim}}(C)}h(x^{-1})}{h(0)}.

Obviously, dim⁡(C)+dim⁡(C⟂)=n.{\rm{dim}}(C)+{\rm{dim}}(C^{\perp})=n.

To make cyclic codes constructed have better parameters, many researchers have considered the construction of BCH codes since it is an important family of cyclic codes with many interesting properties and many BCH codes are also the best linear codes in many cases. Binary BCH codes were introduced by Hocquenghem [2], Bose and Ray-Chaudhuri [3]. Let m≥2m\geq 2 be a positive integer and n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1. Let β\beta be a primitive element of 𝔽2m\mathbb{F}_{2^{m}}. For any integer ii, let mβi​(x){\rm{m}}_{\beta^{i}}(x) denote the minimal polynomial of βi\beta_{i} over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2}, which is the monic polynomial of the smallest degree over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2} having βi\beta^{i} as a root. For any integer 2≤δ≤n2\leq\delta\leq n, define

g(m,b,δ)​(x)=lcm⁡(mβb​(x),mβb+1​(x),…,mβb+δ−2​(x)),g_{(m,b,\delta)}(x)={\rm{lcm}}({\rm{m}}_{\beta^{b}}(x),{\rm{m}}_{\beta^{b+1}}(x),...,{\rm{m}}_{\beta^{b+\delta-2}}(x)),

where bb is an integer and lcm⁡(⋅){\rm{lcm}}(\cdot) denotes the least common multiple of the minimal polynomials mβi​(x){\rm{m}}_{\beta^{i}}(x) with b≤i≤b+δ−2.b\leq i\leq b+\delta-2. Let C(m,b,δ)C_{(m,b,\delta)} with generator polynomial g(m,b,δ)​(x)g_{(m,b,\delta)}(x) denote the binary BCH code with designed distance δ\delta. So far, much research has been done on the dimension of BCH codes with some special designed distances([4], [5], [6]), and the parameters of BCH codes with some special length have also been studied thoroughly([7], [4], [8], [9], [10], [11], [12], [13]). However, there are many kinds of BCH codes that still remain to be investigated.

I-A Related work

Binary cyclic codes have been widely studied for 70 years due to their theoretical importance and practical applications. Many good properties and constructions of binary cyclic codes have been proposed during this time([14], [15], [16],[17],[18],[19],[20]). For binary simple-root cyclic codes, the length nn must be odd. Constructing an infinite family of binary [n,(n±1)/2,d][n,(n\pm 1)/2,d] cyclic codes with large minimum distance dd remains an important and challenging problem. Furthermore, designing a family of binary codes with both a good minimum distance dd and a good dual minimum distance d⟂d^{\perp} presents an even greater challenge. To the best of our knowledge, the known infinite families of binary cyclic codes with large minimum distances can be summarized as follows:

  • •

    Binary quadratic residue codes with parameters [n,(n+1)/2,d][n,(n+1)/2,d] and their even-weight subcodes with parameters [n,(n−1)/2,d+1][n,(n-1)/2,d+1], where d2≥nd^{2}\geq n and n≡±1(mod8)n\equiv\pm 1\pmod{8} is a prime [21]. The lower bound of dd is defined as the square-root bound.

  • •

    The punctured binary Reed-Muller codes of order (m−1)/2(m-1)/2 with parameters [2m−1,2m−1,2(m+1)/2−1][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},2^{(m+1)/2}-1] and d⟂≥2(m+1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m+1)/2}, where mm is odd [22].

  • •

    Two families of binary cyclic codes with parameters [n1​n2,(n1​n2+1)/2,d],[n_{1}n_{2},(n_{1}n_{2}+1)/2,d], where d>max⁡{n1,n2}d>\max\left\{\sqrt{n_{1}},\sqrt{n_{2}}\right\}, n1n_{1} and n2n_{2} are two distinct primes such that n1≡±1(mod8)n_{1}\equiv\pm 1\pmod{8} and n2≡±1(mod8)n_{2}\equiv\pm 1\pmod{8}, or n1≡±3(mod8)n_{1}\equiv\pm 3\pmod{8} and n2≡±3(mod8)n_{2}\equiv\pm 3\pmod{8} [23],[24],[25].

  • •

    A family of binary cyclic codes with parameters[2m−1,2m−1,d],[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d], where m≥3m\geq 3 is odd. If m≡3(mod4)m\equiv 3\pmod{4}, d≥2(m−1)/2+1d\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+1 and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2+2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+2. If m≡1(mod4)m\equiv 1\pmod{4}, d≥2(m−1)/2+3d\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+3 and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2+4d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+4 [26].

  • •

    A family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}-1,d], where m≥4m\geq 4 is even. If m≡0(mod4)m\equiv 0\pmod{4}, d≥2(m−2)/2+1d\geq 2^{(m-2)/2}+1 and d⟂≥2(m−2)/2+2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-2)/2}+2. If m≡2(mod4)m\equiv 2\pmod{4}, d≥2(m−4)/2+1d\geq 2^{(m-4)/2}+1 and d⟂≥2(m−4)/2+2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-4)/2}+2 [26].

  • •

    A family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d], where m≡1(mod4)≥5m\equiv 1\pmod{4}\geq 5. If m≡1(mod8)m\equiv 1\pmod{8}, d≥2(m−1)/2+3d\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+3 and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2+4d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+4. If m≡5(mod8)m\equiv 5\pmod{8}, d≥2(m−1)/2+1d\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+1 and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2+2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+2 [27].

  • •

    A family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d], where m≡3(mod4)m\equiv 3\pmod{4}. If m≡3(mod8)m\equiv 3\pmod{8}, d≥2(m−1)/2+1d\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+1 and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2+2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+2. If m≡7(mod8)m\equiv 7\pmod{8}, d≥2(m−1)/2+3d\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+3 and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2+4d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}+4 [27].

  • •

    A family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d],[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d], where m≥9m\geq 9 is odd d≥3⋅2(m−1)/2−1d\geq 3\cdot 2^{(m-1)/2}-1 and d⟂≥2m−12d^{\perp}\geq 2^{\frac{m-1}{2}} [28].

  • •

    A family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d], where mm is an odd prime, d≥2m−1md\geq\frac{2^{m}-1}{m} and d⟂≥md^{\perp}\geq m [13].

  • •

    A family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [n,≥n+12,d][n,\geq\frac{n+1}{2},d] with length n=∑i=1s(2pi−1)n=\sum_{i=1}^{s}(2^{p_{i}}-1) and d≥⌈n−1∏i=1spi⌉,d\geq\lceil\frac{n-1}{\prod_{i=1}^{s}p_{i}}\rceil, where p1,p2,…,psp_{1},p_{2},...,p_{s} are different primes [29]. However, the value of d⟂d^{\perp} has not been studied.

It is an interesting problem to construct new infinite families of binary cyclic codes with length nn, dimension close to n/2n/2, and both relatively large minimum distance dd and dual distance d⟂d^{\perp}. The following are some known constructions of binary cyclic codes with good parameters in this case.

When mm is even, the construction of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}-1,d] remains underexplored. In [26], it is shown that the lower bound of the minimum distance is 2(m−2)/2+12^{(m-2)/2}+1 for m≡0(mod4)m\equiv 0\pmod{4} and 2(m−4)/2+12^{(m-4)/2}+1 for m≡2(mod4)m\equiv 2\pmod{4} respectively. However, these bounds are smaller than the square-root bound. In [28], Sun et al. constructed a family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1+1−m2,d≥3⋅2m−22+1][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}+1-\frac{m}{2},d\geq 3\cdot 2^{\frac{m-2}{2}}+1], whose dimension is slightly smaller than 2m−1−12^{m-1}-1 as mm increases.

When mm is odd, the punctured Reed-Muller codes have parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d=2m+12−1][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d=2^{\frac{m+1}{2}}-1], in [28], Sun et al. gave a construction of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d≥3⋅2m−12−1][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d\geq 3\cdot 2^{\frac{m-1}{2}}-1]. In addition, when mm is an odd prime, in [13], Sun analyzed a family of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d≥2m−1m][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d\geq\frac{2^{m}-1}{m}], whose minimum distance has lower bound about nlog2⁡n\frac{n}{\log_{2}n}, which is significantly larger than the square-root bound.

I-B Our results

In this paper, we focus on the new constructions of binary cyclic codes with length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1, dimension close to n/2n/2, and both relatively large minimum distance dd and dual distance d⟂d^{\perp}. We summarize our main results as follows:

  • •

    For even mm, we present a new construction of binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}-1,d], where d≥2m2−1d\geq 2^{\frac{m}{2}}-1 and d⟂≥2m2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{\frac{m}{2}}. Compared to the results in [26], our construction achieves improved parameters, with both larger minimum distance and dual minimum distance.

  • •

    For m=p1​p2m=p_{1}p_{2}, where p1p_{1} and p2p_{2} are two different primes, specifically, we present two constructions of cyclic codes with parameters: [2m−1,2m−1,d≥⌊2p1​p2−1p1​p2⌋+⌊2p1−12​p1​p2⌋+⌊2p2−12​p1​p2⌋+⌊2p1−14​p1​p2⌋+⌊2p2−14​p1​p2⌋]\left[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d\geq\left\lfloor\frac{2^{p_{1}p_{2}}-1}{p_{1}p_{2}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{2^{p_{1}}-1}{2p_{1}p_{2}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{2^{p_{2}}-1}{2p_{1}p_{2}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{2^{p_{1}}-1}{4p_{1}p_{2}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{2^{p_{2}}-1}{4p_{1}p_{2}}\right\rfloor\right] when p2>p1≥3p_{2}>p_{1}\geq 3 and [2m−1,2m−1,d≥22​p2−42​p2+2p2−2​p2−24​p2+1]\left[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d\geq\frac{2^{2p_{2}}-4}{2p_{2}}+\frac{2^{p_{2}}-2p_{2}-2}{4p_{2}}+1\right] when p1=2p_{1}=2 respectively. In both cases, the minimum distance dd is much larger than nlog2⁡n.\frac{n}{\log_{2}n}.

  • •

    For odd mm, we present two families of binary [2m−1,2m−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d] cyclic codes with d≥2(m+1)/2−1d\geq 2^{(m+1)/2}-1, d⟂≥2(m+1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m+1)/2} and d≥2(m+3)/2−15d\geq 2^{(m+3)/2}-15, d⟂≥2(m−1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2} respectively. Both the minimum distance and the dual distance of the first family of our codes are no less than those of the punctured Reed-Muller codes. Compared with the binary cyclic codes constructed in [28], which have parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d≥3⋅2(m−1)/2]−1[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d\geq 3\cdot 2^{(m-1)/2}]-1 and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}, the second family of our codes has larger minimum distance while maintaining the same dual distance.

Furthermore, recent research has shown that as the minimum distance dd of a cyclic code CC increases, the value of d⟂d^{\perp} decreases accordingly. The known specific values of dd and d⟂d^{\perp} for binary cyclic codes of length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1 are listed in Tables 1 and 2. In the fifth column of each table, ≈c​n\approx cn means that the lower bound of d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp} is equal to c​n+o⁡(n)cn+o(n) as nn tends to the infinity. Thus, whether we can construct some cyclic codes with both large dd and d⟂d^{\perp} seems to be difficult. In this paper, we construct several families of cyclic codes for which the lower bound of d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp} approached nn in Theorems 7, 10 and 12. Moreover, we present two families of binary cyclic codes with d⋅d⟂≈2​nd\cdot d^{\perp}\approx 2n in Section V. To the best of our knowledge, except the punctured binary Reed-Muller codes, there is no other construction of binary cyclic codes that reaches this bound.

I-C Organization

For the rest of this paper, we present several families of binary cyclic codes of length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1 and dimension k=(n±1)/2k=(n\pm 1)/2. Section II introduces several basic definitions and results. In Section III, we construct an infinite family of binary cyclic codes for even mm. Section IV investigates the case where m=p1​p2m=p_{1}p_{2}, with p1p_{1} and p2p_{2} being distinct primes. Section V studies the case where mm is odd. Finally, Section VI concludes this paper and proposes an open problem regarding the values of d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp}.

II Preliminaries

In this section, we provide some preliminaries that will be used in the subsequent sections. Throughout this section, denote ordn​(i){\rm{ord}}_{n}(i) as the smallest positive integer such that iordn​(i)≡1(modn)i^{{\rm{ord}}_{n}(i)}\equiv 1\pmod{n}. For a binary linear code CC of length nn, we define dim⁡(C){\rm{dim}}(C) and d⁡(C)d(C) as its dimension and minimum distance respectively.

Let ℤn={0,1,…,n−1}\mathbb{Z}_{n}=\left\{0,1,...,n-1\right\} be the ring of integers modulo nn. For any i∈ℤni\in\mathbb{Z}_{n}, the 2-cyclotomic coset Ci(2,n)C_{i}^{(2,n)} modulo nn of ii is defined as

Ci(2,n)={i​2j(modn)|0≤j≤ℓi−1},C_{i}^{(2,n)}=\left\{i2^{j}(\bmod~n)|0\leq j\leq\ell_{i}-1\right\},

where ℓi\ell_{i} is the smallest positive integer ℓ\ell such that i​2ℓ≡i(modn)i2^{\ell}\equiv i\pmod{n}, hence |Ci(2,n)|=ℓi.|C_{i}^{(2,n)}|=\ell_{i}. We define the smallest integer in Ci(2,n)C_{i}^{(2,n)} as the coset leader of Ci(2,n)C_{i}^{(2,n)}. Let Γ(2,n)\Gamma_{(2,n)} be the set of all coset leaders, then we have

ℤn=⋃i∈Γ(2,n)Ci(2,n)\mathbb{Z}_{n}=\bigcup_{i\in\Gamma_{(2,n)}}C_{i}^{(2,n)}

and for any distinct elements a,b∈Γ(2,n)a,b\in\Gamma_{(2,n)}, we have

Ca(2,n)​⋂Cb(2,n)=∅.C_{a}^{(2,n)}\bigcap C_{b}^{(2,n)}=\emptyset.

Let m=ordn​(2)m={\rm{ord}}_{n}(2) and let β\beta be a primitive nn-th root of unity in 𝔽2m\mathbb{F}_{2^{m}}. It is obvious that

xn−1=∏i∈ℤn(x−βi)=∏i∈Γ(2,n)mβi​(x),x^{n}-1=\prod_{i\in\mathbb{Z}_{n}}(x-\beta^{i})=\prod_{i\in\Gamma_{(2,n)}}{\rm{m}}_{\beta^{i}}(x),

where

mβi​(x)=∏j∈Ci(2,n)(x−βj)∈𝔽2​[x].{\rm{m}}_{\beta^{i}}(x)=\prod_{j\in C_{i}^{(2,n)}}(x-\beta^{j})\in\mathbb{F}_{2}[x].

Then mβi​(x)m_{\beta^{i}}(x) is the minimal polynomial of βi.\beta^{i}.

Let CC be a binary cyclic code of length nn with generator polynomial g⁡(x)g(x). Then there exists a subset T⊆Γ(2,n)T\subseteq\Gamma_{(2,n)} such that

g⁡(x)=∏i∈Tmβi​(x).g(x)=\prod_{i\in T}{\rm{m}}_{\beta^{i}}(x).

We define the set Z=∪i∈TCi(2,n)Z=\cup_{i\in T}C_{i}^{(2,n)} as the defining set of CC with respect to β\beta. Then dim⁡(C)=n−|Z|{\rm{dim}}(C)=n-|Z|. From the generator polynomial of C⟂C^{\perp}, we know that the defining set of C⟂C^{\perp} is given by −(ℤn\Z)={−i:i∈ℤn\Z}-(\mathbb{Z}_{n}\backslash Z)=\{-i:i\in\mathbb{Z}_{n}\backslash Z\}. The following is the well-known BCH bound, a fundamental result for cyclic codes.

Lemma 1 ([30]).

Let CC be a binary cyclic code of length nn with a defining set ZZ. If there are integers δ\delta and hh with 2≤δ≤n2\leq\delta\leq n such that {h+i(modn):0≤i≤δ−2}⊂Z\left\{h+i\pmod{n}:0\leq i\leq\delta-2\right\}\subset Z, then the minimum distance d⁡(C)d(C) of the code CC is at least δ\delta.

Let mm be a positive integer. In this paper, we always let n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1. Then for the set

[0,n]={0,1,2,…,2m−1},[0,n]=\left\{0,1,2,...,2^{m}-1\right\},

define

π:[0,n]\displaystyle\pi:[0,n] →𝔽2m\displaystyle\rightarrow\mathbb{F}_{2}^{m}
x\displaystyle x ↦(x0,x1,…,xm−1),\displaystyle\mapsto(x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{m-1}),

where x=∑i=0m−1xi​2i.x=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}x_{i}2^{i}. Clearly, π\pi is a bijection. We define the cyclic shifts of (x0,x1,…,xm−1)(x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{m-1}) as

ρ(x0,x1,..,xm−1)=(xm−1,x0,x1,…,xm−2).\rho(x_{0},x_{1},..,x_{m-1})=(x_{m-1},x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{m-2}).

The following lemma provides an easy criterion for a subset AA of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} to be a union of 2-cyclotomic sets under the action of the map π\pi.

Lemma 2.

Let mm be a positive integer and n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1. Then a subset AA of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} is a union of 2-cyclotomic sets of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} if and only if ρ⁡(π⁡(A))=π⁡(A).\rho(\pi(A))=\pi(A).

Proof:

For any x∈Ax\in A, let π⁡(x)=(x0,x1,…,xm−1)∈𝔽2m\pi(x)=(x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{m-1})\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{m}, where x=∑i=0m−1xi​2ix=\sum^{m-1}_{i=0}x_{i}2^{i}. Then ρ⁡(π⁡(x))=(xm−1,x0,x1,…,xm−2).\rho(\pi(x))=(x_{m-1},x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{m-2}). It leads to π^-1(ρ(π(x)))=x_m-1+∑_i=1^m-1x_i-12^i≡2x ( mod n ) . Suppose AA is a union of some 2-cyclotomic sets of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n}, then for any x∈Ax\in A, we have π−1​(ρ⁡(π⁡(x)))∈Cx(2,n)⊂A.\pi^{-1}(\rho(\pi(x)))\in C_{x}^{(2,n)}\subset A. It leads to ρ⁡(π⁡(x))∈π⁡(A)\rho(\pi(x))\in\pi(A), then ρ⁡(π⁡(A))⊆π⁡(A).\rho(\pi(A))\subseteq\pi(A). Since ρ\rho is a bijection, we can conclude that ρ⁡(π⁡(A))=π⁡(A).\rho(\pi(A))=\pi(A). Conversely, if ρ⁡(π⁡(A))=π⁡(A)\rho(\pi(A))=\pi(A), then π−1​(ρ⁡(π⁡(A)))=A\pi^{-1}(\rho(\pi(A)))=A, which means for any x∈Ax\in A, (2​x(modn))∈A(2x\pmod{n})\in A. We can conclude that Cx(2,n)⊂AC_{x}^{(2,n)}\subset A. Then AA is a union of some cyclotomic sets of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n}.

∎According to the definition of the defining set mentioned above, we have the following Corollary.

Corollary 3.

Let n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1. Suppose Z⊂ℤnZ\subset\mathbb{Z}_{n}. Then ZZ is a defining set of a binary cyclic code with length nn if and only if ρ⁡(π⁡(Z))=π⁡(Z).\rho(\pi(Z))=\pi(Z).

III First Construction: mm is even

In this section, we will consider the construction of binary cyclic codes of length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1 when mm is even. Our method is inspired by the construction of rotation symmetric Boolean functions in [31].

Remark 1.

As far as we know, few studies have focused on binary cyclic codes of length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1, dimension near n/2n/2, and large minimum distance when mm is even. In [26], Tang et al. constructed some binary cyclic codes with parameters [2m−1,2m−1±1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}\pm 1,d] for even mm. We list the parameters of these constructions in the following Table 3. It can be seen that our binary cyclic codes have better minimum distance and dual distance compared to theirs.

Several lower bounds on the minimum distance of binary cyclic codes are given in Table 4. Compared with the square-root bound, the lower bound on the minimum distance of the cyclic codes CC in Theorem 10 is much larger.

V Third Construction: mm is odd

Let mm be an odd integer and set n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1. Recently, considerable research has focused on the construction of binary [2m−1,2m−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d] cyclic codes in this setting, as discussed in [26], [27], and [28]. It is not difficult to observe that as the minimum distance dd increases, the dual distance d⟂d^{\perp} tends to decrease correspondingly. In this section, we present two new families of binary [2m−1,2m−1][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}] cyclic codes with good minimum distance dd and dual distance d⟂d^{\perp}. Notably, the lower bound of d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp} can asymptotically approach 2​n2n.

Sun et al. [28] constructed several infinite families of binary cyclic codes with good minimum distance. In this section, we present a construction of binary cyclic codes that achieve a better lower bound on the minimum distance while maintaining the same lower bound on the dual minimum distance.

Let m>1m>1 be a positive integer and let n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1. For each i∈{0,1}i\in\{0,1\}, denote

S(i,m)={j:1≤j≤n−1,wt(j)≡i(mod2)}.S_{(i,m)}=\{j:1\leq j\leq n-1,wt(j)\equiv i\pmod{2}\}.

Since w​t​(x)wt(x) is constant on each 2-cyclotomic coset Cb(2,n)C^{(2,n)}_{b}, the set S(i,m)S_{(i,m)} must be a union of certain 2-cyclotomic cosets modulo nn. To proceed, we require some known results on the structure of S(i,m)S_{(i,m)} and the coset leaders of 2-cyclotomic cosets.

Lemma 16 ([26]).

Let S(i,m)S_{(i,m)} be defined as above. Then, we have

  • (1)

    If m≥7m\geq 7 is odd, then |S(0,m)|=|S(1,m)|=2m−1−1.\left|S_{(0,m)}\right|=\left|S_{(1,m)}\right|=2^{m-1}-1.

  • (2)

    If m≥6m\geq 6 is even, then |S(0,m)|=2m−1−2\left|S_{(0,m)}\right|=2^{m-1}-2 and |S(1,m)|=2m−1.\left|S_{(1,m)}\right|=2^{m-1}.

Lemma 17 ([11]).

Let m≥7m\geq 7 be odd and ii be an integer with 1≤i≤2m+32−11\leq i\leq 2^{\frac{m+3}{2}}-1 and i≡1(mod2)i\equiv 1\pmod{2}. Then, |Ci(2,n)|=m\left|C^{\,(2,n)}_{i}\right|=m and ii is not a coset leader if and only if i∈{2m+12+1,2m+12+2m−12+1}i\in\left\{2^{\frac{m+1}{2}}+1,2^{\frac{m+1}{2}}+2^{\frac{m-1}{2}}+1\right\}.

The following two lemmas will be used to construct the desired defining set of our binary cyclic codes.

Lemma 18.

Let m≥7m\geq 7 be odd. Then,

Theorem 22.

Let m≥9m\geq 9 be odd. For each i∈{0,1}i\in\{0,1\}, the code C(1,i,m)C_{(1,i,m)} has parameters

[2m−1,2m−1,d≥4⋅(2m−12−4)+1],[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d\geq 4\cdot(2^{\frac{m-1}{2}}-4)+1],

and its dual code C(1,i,m)⊥C_{(1,i,m)}^{\bot} has parameters [2m−1,2m−1−1,d⟂≥2m−12].[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}-1,d^{\perp}\geq 2^{\frac{m-1}{2}}].

Proof:

It is clear that dim(C(1,i,m))=n−|T(1,i,m)|\dim(C_{(1,i,m)})=n-\left|T_{(1,i,m)}\right|. By Lemma 21, dim(C(1,i,m))=2m−1\dim(C_{(1,i,m)})=2^{m-1}, hence dim(C(1,i,m)⊥)=n−dim(C(1,i,m))=2m−1−1\dim(C_{(1,i,m)}^{\bot})=n-\dim(C_{(1,i,m)})=2^{m-1}-1. By (2) and (3) of Lemma 21, the defining set T(1,i,m)T_{(1,i,m)} of C(1,i,m)C_{(1,i,m)} contains the set {j:1≤j≤4⋅(2m−12−4)}\{j:1\leq j\leq 4\cdot(2^{\frac{m-1}{2}}-4)\} and the defining set of C(1,i,m)⊥C_{(1,i,m)}^{\bot} is ℤn\−T(1,i,m)\mathbb{Z}_{n}\backslash-T_{(1,i,m)} which contains the set {j:0≤j≤2m−12−2}\{j:0\leq j\leq 2^{\frac{m-1}{2}}-2\}. The desired lower bound on dd then follows from the BCH bound. ∎

Remark 4.

Compared to the binary cyclic codes constructed in [28], which have parameters [2m−1,2m−1,d≥3⋅2(m−1)/2−1][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d\geq 3\cdot 2^{(m-1)/2}-1] and d⟂≥2(m−1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}, the cyclic codes presented in Theorem 22 achieve larger minimum distance while maintaining the same dual distance.

Remark 5.

In this section, we present two families of binary cyclic codes and both the product of d⋅d⟂≈2​nd\cdot d^{\perp}\approx 2n when nn tends to the infinity. Some specific values of the product of d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp} in recent research have been listed in Tables 1 and 2. Compared with the punctured binary Reed-Muller code R⁡((m−1)/2,m)R((m-1)/2,m) with d⋅d⟂≈2​nd\cdot d^{\perp}\approx 2n, our new binary cyclic codes constructed in Section V-A and Section V-B could be larger than the minimum distance of the punctured binary Reed-Muller code R⁡((m−1)/2,m)R((m-1)/2,m). Moreover, expect the punctured binary Reed-Muller codes, few known constructions have reached this bound to the best of our knowledge.

VI Concluding Remarks

In this paper, we have investigated the binary cyclic code with length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1 and dimension k=(n±1)/2k=(n\pm 1)/2. When mm is even, we provided a construction of binary [2m−1,2m−1+1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}+1,d] cyclic code with d≥2m/2−1d\geq 2^{m/2}-1 and d⟂≥2m/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{m/2}. When mm is odd, we presented two families of binary [2m−1,2m−1,d][2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d] cyclic codes with d≥2(m+1)/2−1d\geq 2^{(m+1)/2}-1, d⟂≥2(m+1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m+1)/2} and d≥2m+32−15d\geq 2^{\frac{m+3}{2}}-15, d⟂≥2(m−1)/2d^{\perp}\geq 2^{(m-1)/2}. When mm is the products of two primes in some cases, we constructed some cyclic codes where dimension is near n2\frac{n}{2} and d>nlog2⁡n.d>\frac{n}{\log_{2}n}.

In recent years, much research has been dedicated to constructing suitable defining sets to make the minimum distance dd of the binary cyclic code CC larger. The known values of dd and d⟂d^{\perp} are listed in Table 1 and 2. However, it seems that the minimum distance dd increases while the dual minimum distance d⟂d^{\perp} decreases correspondingly. For the binary cyclic codes with length n=2m−1n=2^{m}-1, when mm is even and the product of two distinct primes, we construct a family of cyclic codes whose the value of d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp} reaches nn asymptotically in Sections III and IV respectively and when mm is odd. In addition, in section V, we present two families of binary cyclic codes with d⋅d⟂≥2​nd\cdot d^{\perp}\geq 2n asymptotically. To the best of our knowledge, few constructions of binary cyclic codes have reached this bound, even without the condition on the dimension kk. It remains an interesting problem to construct more infinite families of cyclic codes of length nn whose d⋅d⟂d\cdot d^{\perp} has a larger lower bound.

Furthermore, denote Δ=lim supn→∞d⋅d⟂n\Delta=\limsup\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{d\cdot d^{\perp}}{n}, which represents the largest possible value of d⋅d⟂n\frac{d\cdot d^{\perp}}{n} for any family of binary cyclic codes with minimum distance dd, dual distance d⟂d^{\perp}, and code length nn tending to infinity. The punctured binary Reed-Muller codes R⁡((m−1)/2,m)R((m-1)/2,m) and two families of binary cyclic codes constructed in Section V show that Δ≥2\Delta\geq 2. Therefore, we propose the following open problem.

Open Problem :

  • •

    Is Δ>2​?\Delta>2? Equivalently, does there exist an infinite family of binary cyclic codes with minimum distance dd, dual distance d⟂d^{\perp}, and code length nn, such that lim supn→∞d⋅d⟂n>2\limsup\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{d\cdot d^{\perp}}{n}>2?

  • •

    Determine the exact value of Δ\Delta.
